firmographics: Mid-market customer analytics SaaS. Multi-tenant product with heavy customer-facing chat and realtime scoring. HQ: Seattle, WA; primary data residency: US; annual data processed: ~120M events.
commercial_summary: Started on Hosted API for fast proof-of-concept. POC showed good QoE, now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput, lower unit cost and VPC isolation. Negotiating committed capacity, SLA terms and DPA clauses. Procurement timeline targeted Apr 2026.
technical_requirements: Workloads: chat (multi-turn), embeddings for semantic search, reranking for search results. Target latency: p95 <=70ms for chat (512 tokens). Throughput: sustained 150 requests/sec during peak (burst 350). Cost-sensitivity: want 20-30% unit-cost reduction vs. hosted. Model preference: open/quantized variants (Llama-3-ish family), fallback policy to smaller model under congestion.
security_and_compliance_notes: Requires SSO (SAML), KMS integration for encryption-at-rest keys, audit logging retained 1 year by default, DPA wants 30-day deletion guarantees after termination. SOC2 Type II required pre-production access. Legal asks: indemnity limits, liability cap tied to annual fees, data residency clause to restrict EU/UK customer data to region — currently US-only but want future flexibility.
procurement_and_legal_notes: MSA redlines returned 2026-02-03 — primary flags: liability cap (request: 2x ARR -> Redwood original: 1x ARR), termination for convenience (30 days -> Foxglove wants 60), indemnification scope (narrowing), export control clause removal request.
DPA queries: retention windows, subprocessors list, right to audit frequency. Foxglove legal requested explicit KMS/HSM controls and SLA-backed data availability commitments.

SLA negotiation: Foxglove requested uptime credits to apply per-route (chat endpoints) rather than account-wide. Also asked for clearer p95 vs p99 measurement windows and root-cause reporting cadence.
Vendor onboarding checklist: completed security questionnaire v1, submitted SOC2 link (pending redaction review), requested pen-test report (SEC-2209 opened).

SE recommends Dedicated for predictable tail-latency and VPC. Redwood Optimize suggestions: prefix caching, dynamic batching, mixed-quantization models to hit cost targets.
